visual: Dwarf clump-forming saxifrage with scalloped dark green foliage showing pinkish-red tones and variegation, topped in autumn by masses of bright pink star-shaped flowers with contrasting yellow centres.
water: Keep consistently moist during active growth, but ensure excess water drains freely.
aspect: East, south or west-facing; partial to full shade in a sheltered position.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral and alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid hot exposed positions, prolonged drought and stagnant winter water.
prune: No routine pruning required; remove spent flower stems and damaged foliage when necessary.
resilience: Hardy through most of the UK when grown in a sheltered, moisture-retentive but well-drained position.
uses: Shady borders, woodland gardens, rock gardens, containers, courtyard planting and autumn colour.

visual: Slow-growing evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy finely serrated dark green leaves and autumn to winter flowers; cultivated forms range from white and pale pink through to rich rose-pink and may be single, semi-double or double.
water: Keep evenly moist, particularly during summer when flower buds are developing; rainwater is preferable where tap water is alkaline.
aspect: East, north, south or west-facing; sun to partial shade in a sheltered position.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained acidic soil, ideally around pH 5.5–6.5.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline or chalky soil, prolonged drought and cold exposed winds; flower buds may be damaged by severe frost.
prune: Little pruning is normally required; lightly shape after flowering if necessary.
resilience: Hardy through much of the UK in sheltered gardens, though autumn and winter flowers are more vulnerable to severe frost and freezing winds.
uses: Autumn-flowering borders, woodland gardens, sheltered courtyards, containers, wall-side planting and evergreen structure.
uncertain: 'Floraison automnale' is French for 'autumn flowering' and does not identify a cultivar; no cultivar name was present in the supplied label text.
